title: Kirlian Photography: Can Cameras See Your Soul?
description:
Can a camera really capture your soul or aura? For decades, believers in Kirlian photography have claimed that glowing halos in these photos reveal chakras, life force, or even proof of reincarnation. From Hindu ideas of atman and chakras, to Christian, Islamic, and mystical concepts of the soul, the belief in invisible energy fields is ancient.

In this video, Pale Blue Thoughts examines the origins of aura claims, from Charles Leadbeater’s Theosophy to the Soviet inventor Semyon Kirlian’s experiments in 1939. We break down the physics of corona discharge, why Kirlian photos glow like neon signs, and why these patterns depend on moisture, conductivity, and humidity — not mystical energy. We also revisit the famous torn leaf experiment, showing how poor methodology and residue fooled people into thinking plants have souls.

Science shows that Kirlian photos are simply electrified air glowing, the same process behind lightning, spark plugs, and neon bulbs. Auras are illusions — afterimages, retinal effects, or neurological phenomena — not evidence of hidden energies.

If you’ve searched for “Kirlian photography explained,” “aura photography debunked,” “soul photography,” “torn leaf experiment,” “can cameras see auras,” “corona discharge science,” “neon lights and aura photos,” or “why people believe in chakras”, this video uncovers the truth behind the glowing myth.
